mainTopic: Identifying the non-kosher birds of the תורה, with short אגדות along the way, and רב's count of twenty-four non-kosher birds.
overview: This amud keeps going through the list of kosher and non-kosher birds. It gives everyday names and memory hooks for birds like the בת מזגא חמרא and the שקיטנא, and explains the תורה's names שלך and דוכיפת. Along the way there are short אגדות: רבי יוחנן praises ה׳ when he sees a שלך or an ant, and the רחם bird is said to bring rain or even signal משיח. אמימר rules that some birds depend on local custom, and the גמרא explains that the custom guards against mixing them up with the look-alike פרס and עזניה. ברייתות show that the word תנשמת means a bird in one list and a creeping creature in the other, judged by context. They also explain which birds the words עורב, נץ, חסידה and אנפה include. Finally, רב teaches that there are twenty-four non-kosher birds, and the גמרא works to make the תורה's lists add up to that number. אביי's proof that the דאה and the ראה are one bird continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The little wine-pourer bird is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The smaller bird called בת מזגא חמרא is kosher. The memory hook is 'the son is stronger than the father.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'little wine-pourer' bird is permitted. Your memory hook: 'The power of the son is greater than the power of the father.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of birds and rules that the smaller 'daughter' version of the wine-pourer bird is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the larger מזגא חמרא was declared forbidden. Now the smaller 'daughter' bird gets the opposite ruling. The memory hook works because here the 'child' comes out better (permitted) than the 'parent' (forbidden).

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'daughter of the wine-pourer', a smaller kind of that bird
Your memory hook (a mnemonic to help you remember the rule)
The son's power is greater than the father's, a well-known saying used here as a memory hook

steps.confusionAlert: The סימן here is not a reason or a proof for the halacha. It is only a memory trick to help you remember which bird is permitted.

phrases.english: The little wine-pourer bird is permitted,
and your memory hook is: 'The power of the son is greater'
than the power of the father.'
phrases.notes: The small 'child' bird comes out better, permitted, than the big 'parent' bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of birds from before this section, contrasting with the forbidden larger מזגא חמרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בת מזגא חמרא is a kosher bird.

steps.title: Three kinds of שקיטנא birds
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה splits the שקיטנא birds into three types. The long-legged red ones are permitted. The short red ones and the long-legged green ones are forbidden. Each type has its own memory hook.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: The שקיטנא birds. The long-legged red ones are permitted, and your memory hook is the מורזמא bird. The short red ones are forbidden, and your memory hook is 'a dwarf is unfit.' The long-legged green ones are forbidden, and your memory hook is 'green ones are unfit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a three-part guide for telling which שקיטנא birds are kosher, based on leg length and color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two features decide the ruling: leg length and color. Only a bird with both long legs and red color is permitted. If either feature changes (short legs, or green color), the bird is forbidden. Each memory hook links the feature to a familiar idea: the kosher מורזמא bird, a dwarf כהן who is פסול, and green innards that are פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A family of birds whose kosher status depends on their appearance

steps.whatToRemember: For שקיטנא birds, only the long-legged red ones are kosher. Short red ones and long-legged green ones are forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says: The shekitena birds:
the long-legged red ones are permitted,
and your memory hook is the murzema bird.
phrases.notes: The מורזמא is a bird that looks similar and is known to be kosher.

phrases.english: The short red ones are forbidden,
and your memory hook is: 'A dwarf is unfit.'
phrases.notes: A dwarf כהן may not do the עבודה in the בית המקדש. Short means 'unfit'.

phrases.english: The long-legged green ones are forbidden,
and your memory hook is: 'Green ones are unfit.'
phrases.notes: This points to the earlier משנה where innards that turned green make an animal a טריפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of bird identifications with a new bird family.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שקיטנא is permitted only when it is long-legged and red. Short red ones and long-legged green ones are forbidden.

steps.title: What the שלך and the דוכיפת are
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains two non-kosher birds from the תורה's list. The שלך is the bird that scoops fish out of the sea. The דוכיפת is the bird whose crest looks folded over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: The 'shalakh' is the bird that scoops fish out of the sea. The 'dukhifat' is the one whose crest is folded.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains the names of two forbidden birds from the תורה by connecting each name to something the bird does or looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both explanations are wordplay on the bird's name. שלך sounds like שולה (to scoop out), and דוכיפת sounds like הודו כפות (its crest is folded). This helps identify which real-world birds the תורה means.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher bird listed in the תורה (ויקרא 11:17)
A non-kosher bird listed in the תורה (ויקרא 11:19)
Its crest (literally 'its glory') is folded over

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says: The 'shalakh'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:17

phrases.english: is the bird that scoops fish out of the sea.
The 'dukhifat' is the bird whose crest is folded over.
phrases.notes: The name is read as two words: הוד (its 'glory', meaning its crest) and כפות (folded).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: ״שָׁלָךְ״, זֶה הַשּׁוֹלֶה דָּגִים מִן הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from rulings on specific birds to explaining the names of two birds from the תורה's forbidden list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שלך is the fish-scooping bird. The דוכיפת is the bird with a folded crest.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the meaning of דוכיפת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing about the דוכיפת as רב יהודה. It also adds that this is the bird that brought the שמיר to the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: The דוכיפת is the bird whose crest is folded, and this is the bird that brought the שמיר to the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא already said the same explanation as רב יהודה, which supports his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רב יהודה's explanation of דוכיפת word for word, so his explanation has earlier backing. It also adds a new fact: this bird is the one that brought the שמיר for building the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A special creature used in building the בית המקדש

phrases.english: It is also taught in a baraita this way:
The dukhifat is the bird whose crest is folded over,
and this is the bird that brought the shamir to the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's explanation of דוכיפת from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's explanation that the דוכיפת is the bird with the folded crest.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that gives the same explanation and adds the story of the שמיר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reactions to the שלך and the ant
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוחנן saw a שלך, he said 'Your judgments are like the great deep.' When he saw an ant, he said 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן would see a שלך, he would say: 'Your judgments are like the great deep.' When he would see an ant, he would say: 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about the פסוקים רבי יוחנן said when he saw certain creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שלך catches fish deep in the sea, which reminded רבי יוחנן of ה׳'s judgment reaching even the deep. The tiny ant reminded him of ה׳'s kindness, which reaches even the smallest creatures. He split one פסוק into its two halves, one for each creature.

keyTerms.meaning: The great deep, meaning the depths of the sea

steps.whatToRemember: Seeing these creatures led רבי יוחנן to praise ה׳: the שלך showed ה׳'s judgment, and the ant showed His kindness.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי שָׁלָךְ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan, when he would see a shalakh,
would say: 'Your judgments are like the great deep.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 36:7

phrases.english: When he would see an ant,
he would say: 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains.'
phrases.notes: This is the first half of the same פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי שָׁלָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the שלך from step 3 and moves into a short אגדה about רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן praised ה׳'s judgment when he saw a שלך and ה׳'s kindness when he saw an ant.

steps.title: אמימר: two birds are permitted, two depend on custom
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says the לקני and בטני birds are permitted. Whether one may eat the שקנאי and בטנאי depends on local custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר says: The לקני and בטני birds are permitted. The שקנאי and בטנאי birds may be eaten in places where people are used to eating them. In places where people are used to not eating them, they are not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר adds more birds to the list. Two of them are simply permitted, and two depend on what people in that place usually do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, every bird was either kosher or not kosher. Now אמימר introduces a middle group whose status depends on a local מנהג. This sets up the obvious question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where people have a custom
Names of two kinds of birds that are always permitted
Names of two kinds of birds whose status depends on custom

phrases.english: Ameimar says:
The laknei and batnei birds are permitted.
As for the sakna'ei and batna'ei birds:
in a place where the custom is to eat them, they eat them;

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לֶאֱכוֹל אֵין אוֹכְלִין.
phrases.english: in a place where the custom is not to eat them, they do not eat them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of bird identifications from the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לקני and בטני are permitted. Whether שקנאי and בטנאי may be eaten follows local custom.

steps.title: Can kashrus depend on custom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a bird's permission could depend on local custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say the matter depends on custom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised. A bird is either kosher or not, so how can custom decide it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a bird is kosher should depend on the bird itself, not on what people do in a certain town. The challenge is aimed at the second half of אמימר's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a surprised question)

phrases.english: Is that to say that the matter depends on custom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the custom-based ruling in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that שקנאי and בטנאי depend on local custom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Kashrus is a fixed fact about the bird and cannot change from place to place.

steps.title: It depends on whether look-alike non-kosher birds live there
steps.stepSummary: Yes, it depends on the place. Where the non-kosher פרס and עזניה are found, people avoid these birds. Where they are not found, people eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, and it is not difficult. This case is a place where the פרס and עזניה are found. That case is a place where the פרס and עזניה are not found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the custom is not random. It depends on whether non-kosher birds that look similar live in that area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The birds themselves are kosher. But where the non-kosher פרס and עזניה are common, people might mix them up, so the custom there is not to eat them. Where those birds are not around, there is no risk, so people eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: Two non-kosher birds from the תורה's list

steps.confusionAlert: The custom does not make a kosher bird non-kosher. The birds are kosher everywhere. The custom is only a safeguard against confusing them with similar non-kosher birds.

phrases.english: Yes, but it is not difficult:
this is in a place where the peres and ozniyya are found,
phrases.notes: פרס and עזניה are non-kosher birds listed in ויקרא 11:13.

phrases.aramaic: הָא בְּאַתְרָא דְּלָא שְׁכִיחִי פֶּרֶס וְעׇזְנִיָּה.
phrases.english: and that is in a place where the peres and ozniyya are not found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Custom seemed to be deciding whether the bird is kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The custom reflects a real concern about confusion with the non-kosher look-alikes פרס and עזניה, which are found in some places and not others.

steps.title: אביי on the קואי, קקואי and קקואתא birds
steps.stepSummary: אביי says קואי and קקואי are forbidden and קקואתא is permitted. Still, in ארץ ישראל they give lashes to someone who eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: The קואי and קקואי birds are forbidden, but the קקואתא is permitted. In the West they give lashes on account of it, and they call it תחוותא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי identifies three more birds. Two are forbidden and one is permitted. He then notes that in ארץ ישראל people are punished for eating the permitted one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the basic rule, the קקואתא is permitted. Even so, in ארץ ישראל they treated it strictly enough to give lashes, and they called it by a different name. This is another case where a place treats a bird more strictly than the basic law.

keyTerms.meaning: The name used for this bird in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Abaye says:
The kevai and kakvai birds are forbidden,
but the kakvata is permitted.
In the West they give lashes on account of it,
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: and they call it taḥveta.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another bird ruling to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קואי and קקואי are forbidden. קקואתא is permitted, though in ארץ ישראל they give lashes to someone who eats it.

steps.title: The תנשמת among the birds is the באות, learned from context
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the תנשמת in the bird list is the bird called באות. We know it means a bird because the surrounding פסוקים are about birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The תנשמת is the באות among birds. Do you say it is the באות among birds, or is it only the באות among creeping creatures? Say: go and learn from the thirteen rules the תורה is explained by. One of them is that a matter is learned from its context. What are the פסוקים talking about? Birds. So here too, birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא identifies the תנשמת in the bird list as the באות. It then proves that the word means a bird and not a creeping creature, because of where the word appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תנשמת shows up twice in the תורה, once among birds and once among שרצים. The ברייתא uses the rule of דבר הלמד מעניינו: you understand a word by the topic around it. Since this פסוק sits in the bird list, the word here means a bird.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher creature named in the תורה (appears twice)
The common name the ברייתא gives to identify it
The thirteen rules used to explain the תורה
A matter learned from its context

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same word in the תורה can mean two different creatures, and the context decides which one.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The tinshemet is the ba'ut among birds.
phrases.notes: The bird list is in ויקרא 11:18.

phrases.english: Do you say it is the ba'ut among birds,
or is it only the ba'ut among creeping creatures?
phrases.notes: The word תנשמת also appears in the list of creeping creatures, in ויקרא 11:30.

phrases.english: Say: go out and learn
from the thirteen principles
by which the Torah is explained:
a matter learned from its context.
What is the passage talking about?
About birds. So too here, it means birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bird rulings by אמוראים to a ברייתא identifying a bird from the תורה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנשמת in the bird list is the באות among birds, proven from its context.

steps.title: The תנשמת among creeping creatures is learned the same way
steps.stepSummary: A matching ברייתא says the תנשמת in the creeping-creature list is the באות among שרצים, using the same rule of context.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught the same way about creeping creatures: The תנשמת is the באות among creeping creatures. Do you say it is the באות among creeping creatures, or is it only the באות among birds? Say: go and learn from the thirteen rules. A matter is learned from its context. What are the פסוקים talking about? Creeping creatures. So here too, creeping creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that works exactly like the first, but in the other direction. In the creeping-creature list, the context shows that תנשמת means a creeping creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together, the two ברייתות show that the תורה uses one name for two different creatures. Each time, the surrounding פסוקים decide which one is meant. The second ברייתא completes the picture.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two creatures called תנשמת, one bird and one creeping creature. Each is identified from the topic of the פסוקים around it (דבר הלמד מעניינו).

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי גַּבֵּי שְׁרָצִים כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא:
phrases.english: It is also taught in this way regarding creeping creatures:
The tinshemet is the ba'ut among creeping creatures.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:30.

phrases.english: Do you say it is the ba'ut among creeping creatures,
or is it only the ba'ut among birds?
Say: go out and learn
from the thirteen principles
by which the Torah is explained:
a matter learned from its context.
What is the passage talking about?
About creeping creatures. So too here, it means creeping creatures.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי גַּבֵּי שְׁרָצִים כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that applies the same method to the second תנשמת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנשמת in the creeping-creature list is the באות among שרצים, proven from its context.

steps.title: Everyday names for the two kinds of באות
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the common names: the באות among birds is the קיפוף, and the באות among creeping creatures is the קורפדאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The באות among birds is the קיפוף. The באות among creeping creatures is the קורפדאי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the two kinds of באות from the ברייתות just quoted and tells us what people commonly call each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות only told us that the תנשמת is a באות, but not which creature that is in everyday life. אביי fills that in, so a person can recognize each one in real life.

keyTerms.meaning: The name the ברייתא gave for the תנשמת
Common name for the bird kind of באות
Common name for the creeping-creature kind of באות

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The ba'ut among birds is the kifof,
the ba'ut among creeping creatures is the kurpedai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the everyday names for the two באות categories from steps 10 and 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: באות of birds = קיפוף; באות of שרצים = קורפדאי.

steps.title: Identifying the קאת and the רחם
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the תורה's קאת is the קוק, and the רחם is the שרקרק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The 'קאת' is the קוק. The 'רחם' is the שרקרק.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה identifies two more non-kosher birds from the תורה's list by their common names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the job of matching the תורה's bird names to birds people actually know. The רחם mentioned here becomes the subject of the next few steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher bird in the תורה's list
A non-kosher bird in the תורה's list
Common name for the רחם; it sounds like the bird's whistling call

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
"Ka'at" — this is the kuk,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:18

phrases.english: "Raḥam" — this is the sherakrak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: קָאָת זוֹ הַקּוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues identifying birds from the תורה's list.

steps.title: Why the bird is called רחם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the name: when the רחם comes, mercy comes to the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why is it called רחם? Because when the רחם comes, mercy (רחמים) comes to the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains where the name רחם comes from by linking it to the word רחמים, mercy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird's arrival is a good sign, since it comes at the start of the rainy season, and rain is a mercy for the world. The name רחם and the word רחמים share the same root.

keyTerms.meaning: Mercy; here, the blessing of rain
It is called by the name

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Why is it called raḥam?
Because when the raḥam comes,
mercy comes to the world.
phrases.notes: The mercy here is rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ רָחָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the רחם named in step 13 and explains its name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רחם is named for the רחמים (rain) that come with it.

steps.title: When the רחם is a sign of rain, and when it signals משיח
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי limits the rain sign to when the bird sits on something and calls 'שרקרק'. There is also a tradition that if it sits on the ground and hisses, משיח is coming.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: That is only when it sits on something and makes the sound 'שרקרק'. And we have a tradition that if it sits on the ground and hisses, משיח is coming, as it says: 'I will hiss for them and gather them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי narrows רבי יוחנן's statement and adds a second, bigger sign: a רחם hissing on the ground means משיח is coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rain sign only works in one setting: the bird perched on something and calling 'שרקרק'. A different setting, sitting on the ground and hissing, points to the final redemption. The פסוק supports this with the word אשרקה, 'I will hiss', said about gathering the Jewish people.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
And that is only when it sits on something
and makes the sound "sherakrak."
And we have a tradition that if it sits on the ground and hisses,
the Messiah is coming,
as it is stated: "I will hiss for them and gather them."
phrases.notes: זכריה 10:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies רבי יוחנן's statement and adds the tradition about משיח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain sign = sitting on something and calling 'שרקרק'; sitting on the ground and hissing = משיח is coming.

steps.title: A רחם that hissed on a field and was killed
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר שימי asks מר בר רב אידאי about a רחם that hissed on a plowed field, and a stone came and smashed its head. משיח did not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר שימי said to מר בר רב אידאי: But there was a certain רחם that sat on a plowed field and hissed, and a stone came and smashed its head!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר שימי challenges the tradition from a real event: a רחם did hiss on the ground, yet משיח did not come, and the bird was killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition said that hissing on the ground means משיח is coming. Here that happened and nothing came of it. On top of that, the bird was struck down, which makes the whole sign look unreliable.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר שִׁימִי לְמָר בַּר רַב אִידַאי:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Shimi said to Mar bar Rav Idai:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָהוּא דְּיָתֵיב בֵּי כְרָבָא וּשְׁרַק,
phrases.english: But there was a certain one that sat on a plowed field and hissed,
phrases.notes: 'A certain one' means a רחם bird.

phrases.english: and a stone came and smashed its head!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָהוּא דְּיָתֵיב בֵּי כְרָבָא וּשְׁרַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the tradition from step 15 with a real event.
steps.kashyaTarget: The tradition that a רחם hissing on the ground means משיח is coming.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A רחם hissed on the ground, yet משיח did not come and the bird was killed, so the sign seems false.

steps.title: That bird was a liar
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אידאי answers that the bird was a liar, a false sign, and so it was punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That one was a liar.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אידאי answers that the bird in the story gave a false sign. That is why משיח did not come and the bird was struck down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps the tradition in place. A genuine hissing on the ground does mean משיח is coming, but this bird gave a false signal. The stone that killed it was its punishment.

phrases.english: He said to him:
That one was a liar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the case: that bird was a false sign, so the event does not disprove the tradition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story shows the tradition about the רחם hissing on the ground is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: That bird was a liar and was punished; the tradition stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The רחם brings 'mercy' (rain) when it perches and calls 'שרקרק'. Hissing on the ground signals משיח, and the bird that did so falsely was a liar and was killed.

steps.title: Which birds count as עורב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the words of the פסוק: 'עורב' is the crow, 'every עורב' adds the valley crow, and 'after its kind' adds the crow that comes at the heads of pigeons.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'עורב' is the crow. 'Every עורב' comes to include the valley crow. 'After its kind' comes to include the crow that comes at the heads of pigeons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to identifying birds from the תורה's list and quotes a ברייתא that reads each word of the פסוק about the עורב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra word in the פסוק adds another bird to the forbidden group. The basic word gives the regular crow. 'Every' adds the valley crow, and 'after its kind' adds the crow found near the heads of pigeons.

keyTerms.meaning: Crow or raven, a non-kosher bird
To include (something added by an extra word)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Orev" — this is the crow,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:15

phrases.english: "Every orev" — to include the valley crow,
"After its kind" — to include the crow that comes at the heads of pigeons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about the רחם and returns to identifying the birds in the תורה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The forbidden עורב group includes the regular crow, the valley crow, and the crow that comes at the heads of pigeons.

steps.title: How does 'the crow is the crow' help us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line 'עורב is the עורב' and asks how that tells us anything, since no crow is standing in front of us.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'עורב' means the crow. Is it standing in front of us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from the last step and questions its first line. Saying 'the crow is the crow' explains nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was supposed to identify which birds are forbidden. Defining a word by repeating it would only help if we could point at the bird. Since we can't, the definition seems empty and needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Used to push back on a statement that doesn't make sense
It is standing in front of us
The crow or raven, one of the forbidden birds

phrases.english: The Master said: 'Orev' – this is the crow.
Is that to say it is standing in front of us?
phrases.notes: You can't point at it, so just repeating the name tells us nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first line of the ברייתא cited in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's definition 'עורב is the עורב'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Defining a bird by its own name gives no usable information unless the bird is physically present.

steps.title: The plain crow is the black crow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: the plain עורב means the black crow, and brings a פסוק that crows are black.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'עורב' is the black crow. And so the פסוק says: 'His locks are curled, black as a crow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא so it gives real information. The plain עורב is the black one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fix turns an empty definition into a real one by adding a color. The פסוק in שיר השירים shows that black is the color people connect with the עורב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא changes the reading of a source

phrases.english: Rather, say: 'Orev' – this is the black crow,
and so it says:
'His locks are curled, black as a crow.'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 5:11

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא just repeats the bird's name, which tells us nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the black crow, as the פסוק shows crows are known for being black.

steps.title: The valley crow is the white crow
steps.stepSummary: The 'valley' crow from the ברייתא is the white crow, because the word עמוק (deep) is used for something white in the laws of צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The valley crow is the white one. And so the פסוק says: 'Its appearance is deeper than the skin,' like sunlight looks deeper than the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining the ברייתא, now the second kind of crow, the 'valley' crow. It says this is the white crow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עמקי (valley) shares a root with עמוק (deep). In the צרעת פסוק, 'deeper than the skin' describes a white spot, which looks deeper the way a sunny spot looks deeper than a shady one. So 'deep' is tied to white, and the valley crow is the white crow.

phrases.english: The valley crow – the white one,
and so it says:
'And its appearance is deeper than the skin,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:30, about a spot of צרעת.

phrases.english: like the look of sunlight, which seems deeper than the shade.
phrases.notes: A bright, sunny spot looks deeper than a shady one; that's how 'deep' connects to white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the ברייתא of Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'valley crow' included by the פסוק is the white crow.

steps.title: The crow whose head looks like a pigeon's
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the 'crow at the heads of pigeons' does not live with pigeons; its head looks like a pigeon's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the crow that comes at the heads of pigeons: רב פפא said, don't say it comes along with pigeons. Rather, its head looks like a pigeon's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third kind of crow from the ברייתא. רב פפא makes clear what the strange phrase means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'at the heads of pigeons' could be read as a crow that comes along at the front of a group of pigeons. רב פפא rejects that and reads 'heads' literally: this crow's head looks like a pigeon's. So the name describes how it looks, not where it lives.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say: rejecting a possible reading

steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture a crow flying with a flock of pigeons. רב פפא says the phrase is about the shape of the crow's head.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists three kinds of עורב: the black crow, the white 'valley' crow, and the crow whose head looks like a pigeon's.

phrases.english: And the crow that comes at the heads of pigeons,
Rav Pappa said:
Do not say that it comes along at the head of pigeons,
rather, that its head looks like a pigeon's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last item of the ברייתא from Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'crow at the heads of pigeons' is a crow whose head looks like a pigeon's.

steps.title: The נץ and the extra bird in its family
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the נץ is the hawk, and the word 'after its kind' adds a bird called בר חיריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'The נץ' is the hawk. 'After its kind' adds the בר חיריא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next forbidden bird on the list, the נץ. A ברייתא identifies it and adds another bird from the same family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like with the עורב, the word למינהו ('after its kind') adds a related bird to the forbidden list. Here the added bird is the בר חיריא, a name the גמרא will now explain.

keyTerms.meaning: After its kind, a word that adds related birds
A bird added to the family of the נץ

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'The netz' – this is the hawk,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:16

phrases.english: 'after its kind' – to include the bar chirya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the עורב to the next bird in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נץ is the hawk, and למינהו adds the בר חיריא.

steps.title: What is the בר חיריא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which bird the name בר חיריא refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the בר חיריא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: what bird is this? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used a name that was not clear. To know which bird is forbidden, the גמרא needs a more familiar name.

phrases.english: What is the bar chirya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the bird named in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the bird called בר חיריא.

steps.title: אביי: it is the שורינקא
steps.stepSummary: אביי identifies the בר חיריא as the bird commonly called שורינקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is the שורינקא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by giving the bird's everyday name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer swaps the unclear name for one people knew in אביי's time. Now the forbidden bird can be recognized.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird's everyday name, used to identify the בר חיריא

phrases.english: Abaye said: The shurinka.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בר חיריא is the bird known as שורינקא.

steps.title: The חסידה and why it has that name
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the חסידה is the white דיה, called חסידה because it is kind to its fellow birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The חסידה is the white דיה. Why is it called חסידה? Because it does kindness with its friends.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another forbidden bird, the חסידה. רב יהודה identifies it and explains its name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה gives two pieces of information: which bird it is (the white דיה) and why the name fits. The name חסידה comes from חסידות, kindness, because this bird is kind to the others.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden bird, here the white דיה
The white דיה, a kind of bird of prey

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
'The chasida' – this is the white dayya.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:19

phrases.english: Why is it called chasida?
Because it does kindness with its fellow birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: ״הַחֲסִידָה״ – זוֹ דַּיָּה לְבָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next birds in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חסידה is the white דיה, named for its kindness to its fellows.

steps.title: The אנפה and why it has that name
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה continues: the אנפה is the angry דיה, called אנפה because it quarrels with its fellow birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אנפה is the angry דיה. Why is it called אנפה? Because it fights with its friends.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה goes on to the next bird in the same פסוק, the אנפה. He identifies it and explains the name the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of the חסידה. The חסידה is kind to the others, while the אנפה is quick to anger and fights with them, and its name comes from that behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden bird, here the angry דיה

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה pairs two kinds of דיה: the חסידה is the white one that is kind to others, and the אנפה is the angry one that fights with others.

phrases.english: 'The anafa' – this is the irritable dayya.
Why is it called anafa?
Because it quarrels with its fellow birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's statement from Step 26 with the next bird.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אנפה is the irritable דיה, named for quarreling with its fellows.

steps.title: רב: there are twenty-four non-kosher birds
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, רב teaches that there are twenty-four non-kosher birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רב חסדא said in the name of רב חסדא, who said in the name of רב חנן son of רבא, who said in the name of רב: there are twenty-four non-kosher birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רב, passed down through several teachers: the number of non-kosher birds is twenty-four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was identifying individual birds. Now it gives a total number. That number will be checked against the lists in the תורה in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda said
that Rav Chisda said
that Rav Chanan, son of Rava, said
that Rav said:
There are twenty-four non-kosher birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from naming individual birds to giving a total count of non-kosher birds.

steps.title: The number does not match either list in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רב חסדא challenges his father: no list in the תורה adds up to twenty-four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רב חסדא said to רב חסדא: Where do you get this number? If from ויקרא, there are only twenty. If from משנה תורה, there are only twenty-one. And if you say we should add the דאה, which appears in ויקרא but not in משנה תורה, there are still only twenty-two!
steps.whatsHappening: The son asks his father where the number twenty-four comes from. He shows that counting the תורה's lists gives twenty, twenty-one, or at most twenty-two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He checks every possible way of counting. ויקרא gives twenty and משנה תורה gives twenty-one. Even combining the lists by adding the one bird found only in ויקרא, the דאה, gives twenty-two. So רב's twenty-four seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? Where in the תורה is this from?
A non-kosher bird listed in ויקרא
Throw it onto them, add it to the count

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda said to Rav Chisda, his father:
From where is this number?
If from Leviticus, there are twenty;

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּמִשְׁנֵה תוֹרָה – עֶשְׂרִים וְחַד הָווּ,
phrases.english: if from Deuteronomy, there are twenty-one.
And if you would say: the da'ah,
which is written in Leviticus
and is not written in Deuteronomy,
add it to them,
phrases.notes: Literally 'throw it onto them,' meaning add it to the twenty-one in דברים.

phrases.english: there are still only twenty-two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number given in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's count of twenty-four non-kosher birds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting the lists in ויקרא and משנה תורה, even combined, gives at most twenty-two.

steps.title: The four times 'after its kind' add four birds
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers in the name of רב that each 'after its kind' in the lists adds another bird, making four more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what your mother's father said in the name of רב: 'after its kind,' 'after its kind,' 'after its kind,' 'after its kinds.' Here are four more.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains that the extra birds come from the words 'after its kind,' which appear four times in the lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time the תורה says 'after its kind,' it adds another bird to the list, like the בר חיריא added by the נץ in step 23. Four extra birds on top of the plain names is how רב gets past twenty-two.

keyTerms.meaning: After its kind, after their kinds

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him:
This is what your mother's father said
phrases.notes: He means רב חנן son of רבא, the teacher in the chain in step 28.

phrases.english: in the name of Rav:
"after its kind," "after its kind," "after its kind," "after their kinds":
here are four more.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דְּאִמָּךְ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29 by finding four more birds in the verses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds an additional source in the wording of the verses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only birds named outright count, so the total is at most twenty-two.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each 'after its kind' adds a bird, giving four more.

steps.title: Now there are too many: twenty-six
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that twenty-two plus four makes twenty-six, not twenty-four.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there are twenty-six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer overshoots. Twenty-two plus four is twenty-six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer fixed the problem of too few birds but created the opposite problem. Now the count is two more than רב's number.

phrases.english: If so, there are twenty-six!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 30 for producing too high a total.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's answer that the four 'after its kind' add four birds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Twenty-two named birds plus four extra birds equals twenty-six, not twenty-four.

steps.title: אביי: the דאה and the ראה are one bird
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins to reduce the count by saying the דאה of ויקרא and the ראה of משנה תורה are the same bird, and starts to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the דאה and the ראה are one bird. For if you think they are two...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to bring the count down by showing that two names in the lists refer to one bird. He begins a proof that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the דאה in ויקרא is the same as the ראה in משנה תורה, then adding the דאה to the count was a mistake, and the total goes down by one. אביי now sets up a proof: 'if you think they are two,' something will not make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher bird listed in משנה תורה
It is one and the same
If it enters your mind, if you would think

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished yet. אביי's proof, and how the count reaches exactly twenty-four, continue on the next amud.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The da'ah and the ra'ah are one bird.
For if it enters your mind
that they are two different birds,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דָּאָה וְרָאָה אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31 by saying two names in the lists refer to the same bird.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies two names as one bird, which lowers the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The דאה and the ראה are two different birds, so both are counted.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are one bird, so it is counted only once. The proof continues on the next amud.
